CONGA: COntinual Neural Gated Architecture for Long-History Sequential Recommendation

Hoang-Vu Le*, Tuong-Bach-Hy Nguyen*, Bac Le
University of Science, VNU-HCM
ACM RecSys 2026 · Minneapolis, USA
*Indicates Equal Contribution
Paper Code arXiv

Hover or tap a block above for details

CONGA layers three contributions on a modernized SASRec backbone — RoPE for norm-preserving positional encoding, KromHC multi-stream fusion with data-adaptive stream selection, and a TITANS two-phase neural memory — achieving up to +18.7% HR@5 over the strongest baseline on ML-1M.

Abstract

Existing sequential recommendation models rely on absolute positional encodings and fixed context windows, producing two structural failure modes: out-of-distribution degradation on histories longer than the training window, and hard context limits that discard long-range interactions. We present CONGA (COntinual Neural Gated Architecture), which addresses these limitations through three contributions: (1) Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) with a norm-preserving property for any sequence length, accelerated by custom CUDA kernels; (2) KromHC multi-stream fusion with exact doubly-stochastic mixing via Kronecker-product parametrization — where ablation confirms the expressivity gain arises from balanced gradient flow rather than additional parameters — together with a data-adaptive stream selection mechanism that prevents overfitting on sparse corpora; and (3) TITANS neural associative memory adapted to discrete-item recommendation, the first such proof-of-concept, via a two-phase training protocol with a structural forgetting-prevention property: the base encoder is frozen, preserving its short-sequence predictions, while Phase 2 only adds a learned memory term. Evaluated under a rigorous full-ranking protocol across four benchmarks (ML-1M, Beauty, Yelp, Steam), CONGA achieves state-of-the-art performance on long-history benchmarks, with gains up to +18.7% HR@5 on ML-1M — the densest, longest-history dataset where all three failure modes are simultaneously active — and consistent improvements on long-history benchmarks, with competitive results on short-history datasets where the RoPE backbone is the primary driver.

Motivation

SASRec-family models learn absolute position embeddings independently for each index, so any sequence exceeding the training window exposes out-of-distribution positions at test time — a structural defect on datasets like ML-1M, where histories reach 300–600 interactions. Standard attention also scales as O(L²) in sequence length, restricting practical context windows to 200–300 items and forcing a single residual stream to simultaneously capture short-term recency and long-term preference.

Method

CONGA layers three components on a modernized SASRec backbone. Each resolves a specific structural limitation identified in the Motivation section above.

C1 — RoPE: Rotary Positional Embeddings

Rather than adding a learned absolute position vector, RoPE rotates the query/key vectors by an angle proportional to their position (qt = Rθ,t·WQ·et, kt = Rθ,t·WK·et) — an orthogonal, norm-preserving rotation, so ‖Rθ,tx‖ = ‖x‖ for any t, including positions never seen during training. The attention score between positions t and s then depends only on their relative offset (t−s), eliminating the positional out-of-distribution failure mode entirely. Custom CUDA kernel: 5.0× forward / 5.4× backward.

C2 — KromHC: multi-stream fusion

A single residual stream forces one d-dimensional space to jointly encode short-term recency and long-term preference. KromHC (implemented as MHCv2) instead runs M parallel streams, remixed by an exact doubly-stochastic Kronecker-product matrix (Hres = M1(a) ⊗ M2(b)), with the stream count set by a data-adaptive rule keyed to corpus density. Custom CUDA kernel: 5.2× forward / 4.8× backward.

C3 — TITANS: two-phase neural memory

Self-attention still truncates context to the L=300 most recent items. TITANS compresses the entire extended history into a fixed d×d associative memory, updated online from the prediction error, then combines its readout with the frozen encoder's output via a single learned scalar β. Training is two-phase: Phase 1 trains the encoder alone, Phase 2 freezes it and trains only the memory — a structural guarantee that short-sequence predictions are unchanged. Custom CUDA kernel: 13.2× forward / 15.0× backward, the largest speedup of the four kernels.

Qualitative Case Studies

Two case studies on ML-1M illustrate the mechanism behind the long-history gains above.

Model comparison — user uid=2244

User uid=2244 has 362 recorded interactions; only the 5 most recent are visible to the encoder's attention window — a Comedy/Animation cluster. Ground truth is The Godfather (1972, Action/Crime/Drama), buried 357 interactions in the past, far beyond the attention window. CONGA's TITANS memory compresses this extended history into Mt, recovering the dominant Action/Crime signal and ranking ground truth at position 2. DuoRec, relying on contrastive debiasing without long-range memory, only reaches position 4. SASRec, bound by its fixed context window, produces a Top-5 dominated by recent Comedy/Animation and misses ground truth entirely.

Dashed red border marks ground truth (The Godfather). CONGA ranks it #2, DuoRec #4, SASRec misses it entirely.

Effect of TITANS across history length

Comparing CONGA (full) and CONGA (no TITANS) on a short-history user (left, 18 items) and the same long-history user as above (right, 362 items). For the short-history user, both variants rank ground truth at position 1 — with so few gradient updates, the learned scalar β→0 and the memory's contribution is effectively disabled. For the long-history user, CONGA (full) recovers the long-range Action/Crime pattern via Mt and ranks ground truth at position 2, while CONGA (no TITANS) anchors on the recent Comedy/Animation cluster and misses it entirely — directly matching the monotonic gain pattern in the Long-History User Analysis table above.

Dashed red border marks ground truth. Left: short history (both variants rank it #1). Right: long history (only CONGA full recovers it, at #2).
